newsitem.title: IRAN: U.S. should start rapprochement with Iran - papers.
newsitem.headline: U.S. should start rapprochement with Iran - papers.

text.p: The United States should work for rapprochement with Iran after its efforts to isolate the Islamic republic have failed, two Iranian dailies said on Tuesday.

The English-language Tehran Times and Iran News said in editorials that a U.S. decision not to oppose a natural gas pipeline and reported comments by the head of the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) that Iran's nuclear programme was for peaceful purposes were signs of a failed U.S. policy.

Washington said on Sunday its efforts to isolate Iran remained unchanged despite a decision not to oppose the pipeline, which would carry gas from Turkmenistan on the eastern side of the Caspian Sea across a 788 mile (1,268 km) stretch of northern Iran to Turkey and eventually to Europe.
It said it had no grounds under law to oppose the pipeline.

"We are sure that Washington's decision not to oppose the pipeline did not stem from its altruism, rather it sprouted from helplessness, for Washington cannot really oppose a group of countries who are partners in this great project," the Tehran Times said.
It said U.S. sanctions had failed "in deterring other countries from dealing with Iran".

"The inauguration of President Mohammad Khatami will take place within a couple of days. The U.S. must not miss this oppportunity to pave the way for a rapprochement with Iran," the Tehran Times said.

"Iran's conditions are quite clear, the United States must stop interfering in Iran's internal affairs, it must stop its Iran-bashing policy, it must return Iran's frozen assets and it must try to understand and respect the values of the Islamic revolution instead of opposing them blindly.
"By fulfilling these conditions, the U.S. will pave the way for Iran to review its U.S. policy," it added.

Iran News said that comments by the director general of the IAEA Hans Blix during a visit to Iran earlier this month that Iran's nuclear capability was for peace purposes were a "great blow" to the U.S.'s reputation.
Tehran's official IRNA news agency quoted Blix as saying that various inspections of nuclear installations in Iran indicated they were for humanitarian and peaceful purposes.
Washington has accused Iran of seeking to develop nuclear weapons, a charge Iran has repeatedly denied.
"This is the best time for the U.S. to correct its policy towards Iran. If not, Washington will most certainly face more setbacks in its policies," Iran News said.
